summary: This week brought concrete structural shifts to government UAP handling: a new interagency governance board is now coordinating investigations and declassification across federal agencies, while a separate science advisory council has been tasked with helping resolve what officials are calling "the UAP mystery." The third batch of PURSUE files dropped, revealing assessments that China and Russia may have retrieved unknown objects, adding geopolitical urgency to the disclosure picture. On the public engagement side, a planned forum will give lawmakers and whistleblowers a platform to speak directly to citizens, and NewsNation's documentary "Disclosure Day" drew real-world encounter accounts into the mainstream conversation. Meanwhile, questions persist about historical classified programs like MJ-12, declassification timelines tied to an FY2026 NDAA briefing deadline, and whether the Vatican actually holds UFO records.
